analysis.title: Blue Sweep, Red Dollar, Green Equities
key_insights: Democrats took Congress after the midterms, with 228 House seats (218 needed) and 54 Senate seats (51 needed). The asset class reaction so far is risk-on.
S&P 500 is up 1.1% and back near 7,700. US 10-year yields fell 3bps to near 4.90%, and rates are bid by a few basis points across the curve.
The USD is lower across G10. NZD (+70bps), AUD (+63bps) and EUR (+50bps) lead. UBS FX Divergence has the systematic model and the quantamental model at maximum short USD in G10.

The Riksbank hiked 25bps to a 2.0% policy rate. The SEK reaction was muted apart from USDSEK (-35bps). UBS keeps its view for USDSEK and EURSEK lower, flagged originally above 10.0 and 11.30 respectively.

NZ labor data fell sharply (-0.1% vs +0.4% estimate), which first weakened NZD, but the post-midterm pro-risk move overrode it. UBS expects to fade the NZD rally given the surprise RBNZ decision still weighs on positioning.
UBS sees 0.56 or lower in NZD as an asymmetric spot to go long. It still views the December RBNZ meeting as a hike, with about 16bps priced in.

Eurozone October inflation was in line with estimates. Headline rose to 4.0% vs 3.8% prior, and core CPI was unchanged m/m. UBS holds a EUR long view, entered in the systematic model on 10/27 and confirmed in the latest FX Divergence.
